newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-RODMAN MEETS WITH NBA COMMISSIONER STERN.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-RODMAN MEETS WITH NBA COMMISSIONER STERN.

text.p: Tempestuous Bulls forward Dennis Rodman, suspended for kicking a cameraman, stated his case Friday to NBA Commissioner David Stern, who said he would decide next week whether to lift the suspension after the All-Star break.

Rodman has sat out seven games of the minimum 11-game ban imposed by the NBA for kicking courtside cameraman Eugene Amos during a game at Minnesota on January 15. The suspension was to last at least through the February 9 All-Star Game.
"The meeting was constructive," Stern said in a terse statement issued after their talk, "and I will decide next week whether or not Dennis will be reinstated following the All-Star break."

Also present at Friday's meeting were deputy commissioner Russ Granik, NBA Players Association chief William Hunter, Rodman representative Dwight Manley and Dr. Lloyd Baccus, medical director of the NBA/NBPA Player Assistance Programme.
The Rev. Jesse Jackson, who reportedly had offered to participate in talks on behalf of Rodman, did not attend.
Rodman, who was also fined $25,000 by the NBA and directed to undergo psychiatric counselling, has reportedly agreed to a $200,000 out-of-court settlement with Amos.
The suspension is the second longest in NBA history, second only to the 26-game ban given to Kermit Washington of the Los Angeles Lakers for punching Rudy Tomjanovich of Houston in 1977.

It is the second suspension of the season for Rodman, who served a two-game, team-imposed suspension earlier this season for a profanity-laced tirade on the referees in December after a loss to Toronto. That suspension cost him $219,512, or 2/82nd of his 1996-97 salary of $9 million.

The five-time rebounding champion with the multi-coloured hair and multiple tattoos has had numerous run-ins with officials, including the head-butting of a referee last March at New Jersey that earned him a six-game suspension.
Upon his return, he kept his emotions in check and helped lead Chicago to a record 72-10 mark and its fourth NBA title in six years.

The 35-year-old Rodman began his career with the Detroit in 1986 and helped the Pistons win consecutive titles in 1989 and 1990. He was named NBA Defensive Player of the Year in 1990 and 1991 and won the first of his five rebounding titles in 1992.
